counting_rules.body_definition: An actual separately printed ciphertext body or surviving ciphertext fragment. Advertised but absent parts are not invented. Distinct received copies and separately printed parts remain distinct physical sources.
counting_rules.stub_exception: The two literal AAA items at p58 A1/A2 are retained as ambiguous short stubs, outside the 679-body denominator. Their role is not assumed to be an ordinary ciphertext body.
counting_rules.other_material: Cleartext-only entries, header-only entries, explicit missing-part notes, instructional examples, key tables and theory are separate material categories. The other_printed_records lists document material exceptions and are not a census of every header or in-line annotation.
counting_rules.scope_limit: Boundary review is not a full new glyph transcription, proof of key assignment, whole-message assembly, or complete plaintext recovery.

baseline_snapshot.note: A fixed starting snapshot, kept separate from all live coverage computations. Public and local working trees can contain different sets of reviewed editions.

notes: The scan contains printed pages 1, 3, and 5–22; blank printed leaves 2 and 4 are not separate PDF pages.
Figures in pp.6–12 reuse instructional cryptograms and are not new intercepted transmissions.
The technical paper’s internal Appendix I translates a five-by-five numeric transposition example; it is not part of the historical intercept log.
Twelve numbered ciphertexts used in the technical explanation; the key is printed on pp.11–12.
These are separately counted teaching examples, not additional historical traffic or claims of new decipherment.
A separate paper by Alan G. Konheim; its examples use a 5×5 alphabet with numerical coordinates.
Example 1 is introduced on p24; the complete short THE ISSUE OF PERFORMANCE illustration is on pp25–26.
Example 2 introduces an alternative substitution table on p33; later continued examples include explicitly excerpted long ciphertexts on pp36 and 41 and numerical/statistical tables.
Repeated example labels, tables and truncated excerpts are not treated as additional historical intercepted messages. No full reproduction of the paper’s mathematical results is claimed.
The intercepted ciphertext bodies begin on printed p56.
These fifteen printed key tables are represented in data/keys.json; several substitution cells remain unknown.
The count is of printed tables, not complete recovered keys or additional ciphertext bodies.
Cover, title/imprint, publisher introduction, volume contents and final publisher list are outside ciphertext counts.

limits: The OCR retrieval pool contains 788 blocks from printed pp57–230, not 788 physical messages. It can split, merge, omit and misread source bodies.
A source-reviewed or fully fixed algebraic label stream may still contain garbles, uncertain numbers, conditional geometry or word repairs. Neither is a count of fully understood historical messages.
Current coverage must be computed from the live catalogue and current evidence; the fixed baseline must not substitute for it.
